title: Microsoft Maia 300 Shown at OCP 2026
gist: ServeTheHome's OCP 2026 look at Microsoft's Maia 300 node: eight HBM4 stacks for 288GB at 18TB/s, 950W accelerators, 96 per rack with a roughly 12K scale-up domain, a cable-heavy hybrid liquid/air design that contrasts with Nvidia's fewer-cable direction.

insights.claim: Microsoft's Maia 300 uses eight HBM4 stacks for 288GB of memory, 18TB/s of memory bandwidth and 3.2TB/s of bidirectional scale-up bandwidth.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Raises the bar for in-house hyperscaler accelerators and supports HBM4 demand.

insights.claim: Microsoft says it fits 96 Maia accelerators into a rack and roughly 12K in the scale-up domain.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Large scale-up domains indicate Microsoft is targeting rack-scale competition with Nvidia NVL systems.

insights.claim: Maia 300 accelerators are 950W TDP parts under liquid-cooled cold plates, and the tray components exceed 4kW with 24 trays per rack.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Power density per rack keeps pushing liquid cooling and power distribution suppliers.

insights.claim: The Maia 300 node is not all liquid cooled: CPU, SSDs, OCP NIC 3.0 devices and components around the accelerators are cooled by a large fan partition spanning the chassis.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Hybrid cooling means air-cooling content remains in AI racks.

insights.claim: Microsoft's Maia 300 is cable-heavy, with each accelerator on its own PCB and multiple cables, whereas Nvidia is designing Vera Rubin NVL72 nodes to use fewer cables.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Cable-intensive designs favor interconnect and cable assembly vendors; Nvidia's approach shifts content elsewhere.
insights.quote: Whereas NVIDIA is designing its Vera Rubin NVL72 nodes and infrastructure to use fewer cables, Microsoft is all-in on cables

insights.claim: The node is about 1.5x standard OU width, narrower than the double-wide AMD Helios, reflecting custom rack and ASIC co-design.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Custom rack form factors fragment the open-rack ecosystem.

insights.claim: The author speculates that selling Maia in a DGX Station-style developer tower would require Microsoft to build a developer ecosystem and commercialize the chip, which it has not done.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Low probability; would signal Microsoft competing in merchant accelerators.

insights.claim: Maia 300 is described as Microsoft's new in-house AI acceleration platform, with the Maia 200 deep-dive presented at Hot Chips 2026 a few weeks earlier.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Cadence of annual Maia generations shows sustained custom silicon commitment.
